chapter: Back to the horn: house sessions
title: Tony Fuggera and the German dance
summary: Tony knows every tune and played German numbers for a crowd who bought him beer.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, it's hard to find a drummer player that knows them now, though. There aren't too many of them, you know. The good ones are working steady. Yeah.
I tell you a boy knows them all, that Tony Fuggera. Oh, yeah. You can't mention any of them that he don't know. That son was going to play any kind of tune, German tunes. He's a guy.
He's a guy. He's a guy. Was it you who was telling me about going to a German dance or something?

At the Dutchess House. He was playing out there. And the Germans come to him and ask him, do you know them German numbers? He said, sure. He said, play. So he started playing them German. And then the German was dancing around. Going nuts. They were buying him more beer than he could consume.

Yeah, because he can consume some beer. Smoke some cigars, too. And eat some. You know, when Tony gets loaded, he gets crying, Jags. You ever eaten one of the crying kicks? He's a character. The only boy that could consume a beer was Bill Wally. Man, when I had them sessions at Mars, I used to order a case of beer extra for Bill. I know he'd drink damn near a case of beer.
